title: Rosemary
html_source:
“Rosemary is for remembrance” says Ophelia in Act 4, Scene 5, line 199 in the Folger Hamlet. In this scene, Ophelia, driven mad by the death of her father and Hamlet’s torments, hands out flowers to members of the court.

As Ophelia is remembering her father, here Bloom is remembering his grandfather. There is also the resonance of rosemary with the flower-names: Bloom, Virag (flower in Hungarian), and Bloom’s alias Flower.
